core_obligations: Rewrite the cartesian property as exactness of the sequence 0 to B' to B direct sum R' to R (proof lines 421-426).
Identify the localisations of B, R' and R at the corresponding elements with the localisations at the element h of B' (proof lines 426-431).
Use exactness of localisation to obtain the exactness of the localised sequence and conclude that the localised diagram is cartesian (proof lines 431-435).
proof_roadmap: Turn the cartesian square into an exact sequence (proof lines 421-426).
Localise the exact sequence and conclude (proof lines 431-435).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the cartesian property of a diagram of rings is preserved by localising at elements that correspond under the two maps, and the proof is a 15-line argument that rewrites the cartesian property as exactness of a two-term sequence and then localises. It observes that the fibre product is the kernel of the difference map from B direct sum R' to R, identifies the localisations of B, R' and R at the relevant elements with their localisations at the element of the fibre product, and concludes by exactness of localisation. The identification of the three localisations is the substance, and it is displayed.
